extra.message: JWT signature verification disabled on /get endpoint — Complete authentication bypass allowing forged tokens to access any customer record [verified: insecure_verify calls jwt.decode(token, verify=False) with no signature/secret check, so any forged token is accepted for /get.]

Auth bypass + IDOR chained on /get/<cust_id> endpoint — Attacker with no valid credentials (any garbage token) can retrieve any customer's PII and credit card number by id [verified: insecure_verify() (app.py:96-99) calls jwt.decode(token, verify=False) and always returns True regardless of signature/validity, and get_customer() (app.py:221-238) uses it as the sole gate before Customer.query.get(cust_id) with no ownership check. Any request with an arbitrary Authorization value bypasses auth entirely and can enumerate any customer's PII and credit card number by id.]

SQL Injection in /search endpoint — Full database read/write, authentication bypass, data exfiltration of customer PII and credit card numbers via UNION-based or boolean/error-based injection [verified: search_term from JSON is directly interpolated into SQL string executed via db.engine.execute with no sanitization; only a JWT check gates it, not input validation.]

Unsafe YAML deserialization in /yaml_hammer — Remote code execution on the server via crafted YAML payload [verified: yaml.load(y) is called with no Loader argument (defaults to unsafe full loader in the vulnerable pyyaml version used here), allowing arbitrary object deserialization from uploaded file content.]

SSTI/XSS via render_template_string with unescaped request data — Reflected XSS or full server-side template injection leading to remote code execution via Jinja2 payloads in the URL or search term [verified: pnf() interpolates request.url via %s directly into a template string then calls render_template_string, so a crafted URL containing Jinja syntax is compiled as a template — SSTI/XSS.]

Plaintext storage of customer passwords and credit card numbers — Full plaintext credential and PCI-sensitive data exposure if the database is read (e.g. via SQL injection), enabling credential stuffing and card fraud [verified: Customer.password and ccn are stored directly from client input with no hashing at all in reg_user, confirmed plaintext persistence of credentials and card numbers.]

IDOR on customer lookup endpoints — Any authenticated user can enumerate and read any customer's PII and credit card number by iterating IDs [verified: fetch_customer/get_customer only check JWT validity, never compare the JWT 'user' claim to the requested customer_id, so any authenticated user can access any record.]

SSTI via error page in /search — Attacker-controlled search_term can inject Jinja template syntax into the error page reflected via render_template_string, leading to RCE [verified: The exception message (which echoes the attacker-controlled search_term embedded in the failed SQL string) is interpolated into a template and rendered with render_template_string, enabling SSTI via crafted search input.]

XXE via DOCX upload processing — Server-side file disclosure, SSRF, or DoS via crafted DOCX/XML external entities [verified: Document(file_path) parses uploaded DOCX via lxml without disabling external entity resolution, and the file is saved/parsed with no content validation.]

Hardcoded JWT/session secret keys — Attacker with source/repo access can forge valid JWTs for any user and forge signed Flask session cookies [verified: secret_key and SECRET_KEY_HMAC/_2 are hardcoded literal strings in source used for session and JWT signing, enabling forgery if source leaks.]

Weak password hashing (MD5, unsalted) — Offline cracking of stored password hashes if the database is exfiltrated (e.g. via the SQLi above), leading to full account compromise [verified: reg_customer hashes User passwords with unsalted hashlib.md5, a broken algorithm for credential storage.]

No rate limiting or lockout on login endpoint — Attacker can brute-force user/customer credentials via unlimited automated login attempts, leading to full account takeover. [verified: login() has no attempt counter, delay, or lockout around the User.query.filter_by credential check, allowing unlimited brute-force attempts.]

Unrestricted file upload processed by vulnerable parsers — Attacker can upload arbitrarily large or malicious files that are then parsed by vulnerable DOCX/YAML handlers, chaining into XXE/RCE and disk exhaustion DoS [verified: Both upload endpoints save any file via secure_filename with no extension/size/content-type allowlist before parsing, permitting malicious or oversized files.]
